solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Here's the best place to start on grid

definitions.text: Here's the best place to start on grid

parts.words: Here's the best place to start on grid
parts.note: a motor-racing grid, where the fastest qualifier takes the front slot at the start of the race

explanation.surface: Advice to a crossword solver on which square of the grid to tackle first.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'grid' looks like the crossword itself, but it is the starting grid of a motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing the leading slot on the starting grid, earned by the fastest qualifier, carries this name.

clue.text: Drug den creates depression in street

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
a hole is a squalid den or lair

explanation.surface: A drug den is causing a slump in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' reads as low spirits, but it is a dip in the road surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit worn into a road surface is exactly a hollow in the street.

clue.text: Section of coil is somewhat flexible

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece of coiled wire is fairly bendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe and supple, a body that bends easily is flexible.

clue.text: Get into exercises with clear speed

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
to net is to clear as profit
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Advice to get fit with exercise done at a fast pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' is the verb, to make a net profit.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce or enter something is to get into it; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Fly around tail-end of the sun

indicators.note: around tells us the flying word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: to soar is to fly high
the end letter of the word tail is L

explanation.surface: An insect buzzing round the tail of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail-end' means the last letter of 'tail'; the definition is 'of the sun', an adjectival phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for anything belonging to or coming from the sun, as in solar power.

clue.text: Magazine say, for gossip

indicators.note: say marks that the word is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Tatler is a British society magazine

explanation.surface: A society magazine is a byword for gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: TATLER is a long-running British society magazine; the answer sounds the same but has a double T.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tells tales and spreads rumours is a gossip, the noun sense.

clue.text: Battle of Vladivostok, in a war

indicators.note: of signals the answer is taken from within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the city name through the next three words

explanation.surface: A naval battle fought off a Russian port during a war.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a battle at Vladivostok; the answer is a 1945 battle on a Japanese island.
explanation.definitionFit: A major 1945 Pacific campaign fought on a Japanese island bears its name.

clue.text: Take off after start of flight here?

definitions.text: Take off after start of flight here?

indicators.note: after places the stripping word behind the stairs word

parts.note: a landing is where a flight of stairs begins or ends
to strip is to take off clothes

explanation.surface: An airfield runway where aircraft leave the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' reads as an aircraft leaving, but means undress; 'flight' is a staircase as well as a journey by air.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is the place where an aircraft begins or ends its journey by air.

clue.text: Thatcher perhaps and supporter losing head

indicators.note: losing head says the front letter is dropped

parts.note: a partisan is a committed supporter

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher and a backer who has been beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thatcher' looks like the prime minister, but it is a roof-thatcher, an example of a craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof thatcher is a skilled manual worker, a craftsman, given as an example.

clue.text: Element ignited with smell containing iodine

parts.note: lit means ignited

indicators.note: containing says the smell word holds the next piece

parts.note: hum is slang for a bad smell
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A chemical element was set alight with an iodine smell.
explanation.walkthrough: HUM is British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic number three, the lightest metal, is a chemical element.

clue.text: Actors turning to ladies' men around one?

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters wrap the next piece
turning says the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Actors who become womanisers when one is near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' rearranges TO LADIES MEN, and 'around' puts I (one) inside that rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart-throb film stars of the silver screen were stage and screen actors.

clue.text: Academic has work with absent failing student

parts.note: Dr is the title of a doctor, an academic
op is short for opus, a work
out means away, absent

explanation.surface: A lecturer and his work, with a student who keeps failing to turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abandons a course of study before finishing is a failed student.

clue.text: Producer of Robin's first line at works

definitions.text: Producer of Robin's first line at works

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the name Robin
works says the letters of line at are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: The car maker's first Robin coming off the production line at the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reliant Robin was a British three-wheeled car; 'Robin' serves both the definition and the first letter, so the clue is semi-&lit. 'Works' rearranges LINE AT to ELIANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The British firm that built the three-wheeled Robin car was a motor manufacturer.

clue.text: Relation's pleasant embracing sweetheart

indicators.note: embracing says the pleasant word holds the next piece

parts.note: nice means pleasant
the heart of the word sweet is E

explanation.surface: A relative is lovely and is hugging a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' is the middle letter of 'sweet', not a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family relation.

clue.text: Discover an act is performed including Queen

indicators.note: including says the rearranged letters take in the next piece
performed suggests the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Finding out that a show is staged in front of the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performed' rearranges AN ACT IS to ASCTAIN, and 'including' puts ER inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out for certain is to discover; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Whip a crew holding middle of oars in ship

parts.note: the cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip

indicators.note: holding says the crew word contains the next piece

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it

indicators.note: middle of takes the centre letters of oars

explanation.surface: Whipping a crew who keep rowing aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew' here is the verb, to man.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-hulled sailing vessel is a kind of boat or ship.

clue.text: A crowd's addressed outside for ceremony

indicators.note: outside says the sent word goes round the rest

parts.note: a letter addressed somewhere is sent
to cram is to crowd in

explanation.surface: A crowd is spoken to in the open air at a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Addressed' reads as spoken to, but means posted, as a letter; 'crowd' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious rite such as baptism or communion is a solemn ceremony.

clue.text: Repairman found at last?

parts.note: a last is the foot-shaped block on which a shoe mender works

explanation.surface: Relief that someone has finally turned up to fix things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' reads as finally, but a last is the shoemaker's form.
explanation.definitionFit: A mender of shoes works at a last, so he is a repairman found there.

clue.text: A non-drinker winds up escorts

parts.note: TT is teetotal, a non-drinker
ends means winds up, finishes

explanation.surface: A teetotaller ends up acting as a chaperone.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany or wait upon someone is to escort them, the verb sense.

clue.text: Opening of 'Bambi' in story board

indicators.note: in says the next piece goes inside the story word

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: Opening of takes the first letter of Bambi

explanation.surface: The start of Bambi on a storyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story board' looks like one film-making term but splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A table is a flat board on legs, and board once meant a dining table, as in bed and board.

clue.text: Playing flute penning a French musical

indicators.note: penning says the rearranged letters enclose the next piece
playing suggests the letters are moved around like notes

parts.note: un is French for a

explanation.surface: Playing a flute while composing a French musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges the flute's letters to TEFUL, which 'penning' wraps round the French article; 'musical' looks like a show but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodious and pleasant to hear means musical, an adjective.

clue.text: Skinhead that is supporting supporters' club

indicators.note: supporting, in a down clue, puts the following pieces beneath the garments

parts.note: bras are supporting garments
the head of the word skin is S
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A skinhead is backing a fans' football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a football club, but it is an old golf club with a brass sole.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned golf club with a brass sole, roughly a two-wood.

clue.text: Automatic rifle with jerk bagging duck

indicators.note: bagging says the outer pieces capture the next one

parts.note: to rifle is to search and steal, rob
a tic is an involuntary jerk
a duck is a zero score in cricket, O

explanation.surface: An automatic rifle with a jerk while bagging a duck on a shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' looks like a gun but is the verb, to rob.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting mechanically without thought is behaving like a machine, automatically.

clue.text: Canine, often royal, grows intimate initially

definitions.text: Canine, often royal, grows intimate initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A royal dog becomes close to its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen famously kept many of these Welsh dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged Welsh dog famously kept by the Queen is a canine often royal.

clue.text: Roof bloke's fit with top off

parts.note: man's means belonging to a bloke

indicators.note: with top off says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: hard means physically fit, tough

explanation.surface: A bloke fitting a roof with the top missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' is an adjective, physically hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof with two slopes on each side, the lower one steeper, is a type of roof.

clue.text: Returning about noon, sink lager

indicators.note: returning says the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to slip is to sink or decline

explanation.surface: Coming home around midday and downing a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns RENSLIP backwards; 'sink' looks like drinking a beer but is the verb to slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale Czech-style beer is a kind of lager.

clue.text: Denial from fellow American in concrete

indicators.note: in says the next pieces go inside the concrete word

parts.note: concrete means real, tangible

explanation.surface: A rebuff from an American colleague, set in concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' looks like the building material but is the adjective, real.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no to a request is a rejection or denial.

clue.text: Paul Rubens is spreading paint colour

indicators.note: spreading suggests the letters are spread around into a new order

explanation.surface: The painter Rubens is applying paint across a canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: Rubens the painter makes the surface feel like art; his name is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep blue pigment made from iron cyanide is a classic paint colour.
